newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada hopes for stronger market.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada hopes for stronger market.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said Wednesday that it hopes for stronger pulp and paper markets by mid-year.

"The prospects for improvement in pulp and paper markets by mid-1997 are favourable, as demand is recovering in the paper sector and customer inventories of pulp and paper are down to more moderate levels," Fletcher president Doug Whitehead said.
The forest company has scheduled a US$75 per tonne newsprint price increase effective March 1.

Fletcher earlier reported a loss of C$0.06 a share in its second fiscal quarter to December 31 after a C$0.12 a share charge for restructuring. This compared with a profit of C$0.56 a share a year earlier.

It said paper prices were under pressure in the quarter as both producers and end-users reduced inventory. But paper consumption began to strengthen and customer inventory levels moderated. Paper shipments were up from the previous quarter.
Prices in the company's main western North American newsprint market fell an average of US$75 a tonne from a quarter earlier.
